Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Storage:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Blox Fruits-inspired game with fruits, swords, quests, bosses, enemies, and exploration across 30 islands in 2 seas.

## Requirements
- Max level 600; 15 islands per sea.
- Include two fruits from each rarity, plus an inventory for fruits and swords.
- Include quest dealers for bosses and normal enemies.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with original, stylized island art and familiar fruit/sword concepts rather than connecting to or copying Roblox game assets.
- Made all 30 islands freely accessible through an atlas; boss encounters can reward swords.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a Three.js island scene, player movement, combat, fruit abilities, inventory, dealer, quest board, stats, and responsive touch controls.
- Added 30 named islands split into First Sea and Second Sea, 15 each.
- Added 10 fruits (two each across Common, Uncommon, Rare, Legendary, and Mythical rarities), swords, normal-enemy hunts, and boss bounties.
- Ran the game in Playwright, confirmed no console errors after reload, and verified the island atlas shows 15 islands for a sea.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Optionally do a final quick pass over the boss/quest reward flows and combat interactions.
2. Summarize the finished game and assumptions to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Full game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The latest verification screenshot is `screenshots/latest.jpg` (ignored by Git).
- Local testing used `python3 -m http.server 3002` and `playwright-cli`; initial browser installation was resolved.

content.text:
Implemented the playable browser game in `index.html`.

It includes 30 islands across two seas, 10 fruits spanning five rarities, fruit and sword inventories, enemy hunts and boss bounties, combat and abilities, progression up to level 600, and keyboard and touch controls. The game was tested in-browser, with no console errors after reload.

Assumptions: islands are freely accessible through the atlas, and the game uses original stylized art and familiar fruit/sword concepts rather than Roblox assets. Changes are uncommitted.
